Survival along a record of temperature, averaged over several fitted models

Source: R/predict-survival.R
average_survival.Rd

Predicts survival along a record as predict_survival() does, averaged over several models fitted to the same data. Each model's posterior draws are pooled in proportion to its weight and the pool is summarised, so the credible intervals reflect both the uncertainty within each model and the uncertainty about which model holds. This matters most where the record lies outside the temperatures of the assay, where failure-rate functions that fit the data equally well can predict very differently (see predict_survival()).

Usage

average_survival(
  fits,
  weights,
  record,
  newdata = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  prob = 0.95,
  n_draws = 1000,
  grid_dT = 0.1
)

Arguments

fits

A named list of brmsfits, models fitted with fit_hazard() to the same data.

weights

The weights from hazard_weights(), whose model names are names of fits. Only the models it kept are averaged.

record

A data frame with the columns time and temp, the record of temperature through time, in the time unit and temperature scale of the data the model was fitted to, with times increasing and no gaps. It may also hold the column of a co-stressor and the column named in by.

newdata

A data frame of covariate values, one row per setting at which to derive. It must hold every covariate in the model's parameter formulas. May be NULL for a model without covariates.

levels

A named numeric vector giving the level of each co-stressor, on its measurement scale, e.g. c(DO = 6). Required when the model has co-stressors.

by

A character string, the name of a column of record giving the period each reading belongs to (e.g., a day). When given, the result has each period's share of the hazard accrued over the record. An interval between two readings belongs to the period of the first.

prob

A single number strictly between 0 and 1, the coverage of the credible intervals.

n_draws

A single number, the number of posterior draws in the pool. Each model contributes its share of them, evenly spaced through its posterior. Where a model holds fewer draws than its share, the pool is made smaller so that the shares stay in proportion to the weights, and a message says so.

grid_dT

A single positive number, the largest change in temperature within a step along the record, in degrees. Between two readings the temperature is taken to change linearly, and the hazard is accrued in steps over which it changes by at most this much, since the failure rate at the midpoint of a step stands for the whole of it (see The time grid in build_hazard_data). Defaults to 0.1; Inf takes one step between consecutive readings.

Value

The list predict_survival() returns, with weights, the table of weights with the number of draws each model contributed. In coverage, the shares of the risk are those of the pooled draws.

Details

The weights say how well each model predicts failures within the assay. They do not say which model extrapolates better below it, which the data cannot tell.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# a model fitted to a small ramping trial: 20 individuals warmed from 20 to 35
# degrees over 60 minutes and checked every minute, in two trials (see fit_hazard())
path   <- data.frame(path_id = "A", time = c(0, 60), temp = c(20, 35))
checks <- data.frame(path_id = "A", time = seq(0, 60, by = 1))
ind    <- data.frame(id = 1:20, path_id = "A", event = 1, mass = runif(20, 8, 12),
                     trial = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 10),
                     t_upper = sample(seq(10, 60, 10), 20, replace = TRUE))
long   <- build_hazard_data(ind, path, "interval", covariates = c("mass", "trial"),
                            checks = checks)
fit_mem     <- fit_hazard(long, "exp", dpar_formulas = list(loga = ~ 1 + mass))
fit_weibull <- fit_hazard(long, "exp", baseline = "weibull",
                          dpar_formulas = list(loga = ~ 1 + mass))
fits        <- list(memoryless = fit_mem, weibull = fit_weibull)
# a two-day record read every hour, with a daily cycle
hours  <- 0:48
record <- data.frame(time = hours * 60, day = pmin(hours %/% 24, 1),
                     temp = 24 + 3 * sin(2 * pi * (hours - 9) / 24))

w    <- hazard_weights(lapply(fits, loo_hazard))
average_survival(fits, w, record, newdata = data.frame(mass = 10))$mortality
} # }
